notes: Entry point, modelled on book ex4-7-6a. The y-coefficients are already opposite (+q and -q) so one addition eliminates y; no multiplying is needed. Sign pattern is fixed in the template (+ in the first equation, - in the second), so all coefficients in the holes are positive and 2 or more (no printed '1x'). r != p keeps adding as the only direct route (if the x-coefficients were equal, subtracting would also work). x and y are non-zero integers in [-6, 6], so answers are whole numbers and may be negative; the determinant -q(p+r) is never zero, so the solution is unique. I checked all about 33,000 admissible parameter sets: x*(p+r) equals the added right-hand sides and q*y equals k1 - p*x in every one. Right-hand sides may be negative, as in the book question.
